***New programme helps tackle skills shortages in maritime engineering by equipping students with industry relevant STEM skills, recognised qualifications and real-world experience***


**PLYMOUTH** (November 19, 2026) — Students at Tor Bridge High School in Plymouth, part of the Ted Wragg Trust, are set to take part in a pioneering STEM skills initiative through a new partnership between trusted global infrastructure consultancy AECOM and social enterprise Class of Your Own.


The programme will provide students with hands-on maritime engineering experience while working towards recognised qualifications, helping them develop valuable STEM capabilities and gain insight into career opportunities across the maritime sector.


AECOM, which has had a presence in Plymouth for more than 20 years and supports a range of maritime clients in the region, has partnered with Class of Your Own to develop an innovative learning programme. Designed to help build a pipeline of future talent in a critical area of engineering facing skills shortages, the initiative will give students aged 12 and above a practical insight into what it takes to plan, design and build a ferry port and community marina, while highlighting career opportunities in an industry that plays a vital role in the region’s economy.


Supported by engineers from AECOM and global defence and engineering company Babcock International Group (Babcock), students will take on the challenge of designing a port facility that meets the needs of both the local community and the environment, applying real-world engineering principles. Working as a professional design team, students will explore the geography and topography of a coastal site, investigating factors such as tides, water depth, wind conditions, wave patterns, and hydrology. They will also consider how people, goods and vessels can move safely and efficiently through the port environment, as well as examine the broader economic, environmental and social role a modern port can play within its community.


Tracy Stephenson, Headteacher at Tor Bridge High, said: “This partnership gives our students the opportunity to work on a substantial and highly relevant engineering project connected to the maritime identity of Plymouth.


“They will be applying maths, geography, science, design and digital skills to a real challenge, supported by professionals from AECOM and Class Of Your Own. It will help them understand why their classroom learning matters and where it could take them in the future.”


Gemma Maynard, Senior Maritime Engineer, AECOM, said: “This is a fantastic initiative that addresses a real industry challenge by helping to develop the skills our sector needs for the future. Through designing their own port facility, students will gain first-hand experience of how STEM subjects are applied in real-world engineering projects and the vital role that ports play in supporting communities and economic growth.


“Our engineers will volunteer their time through our social value programme to work directly with the students, sharing their expertise, providing mentorship and offering a first-hand insight into the opportunities a career in engineering can provide. The initiative is designed to raise awareness of careers in marine engineering and related industries, helping to create a pipeline of skilled professionals for the future. Maritime industries have a long heritage in Plymouth, and developing a strong pipeline of local talent will be vital to supporting their continued growth, innovation and contribution to the region’s economy.”


Alison Watson MBE, founder and CEO of Class Of Your Own and creator of Design Engineer Construct!, said: “As a former land surveyor with a lifelong passion for geospatial engineering, I am particularly excited to see Tor Bridge students exploring the relationship between land and water through this project.


“A successful port begins with a detailed understanding of topography, hydrology, tides, levels and movement. By using geospatial data and digital twin technology, students will be able to investigate a real place, test their decisions and see maths become an essential design tool.


“This is what meaningful built environment education should look like. Students are trusted with a genuine context, teachers are supported by industry, and learning is connected directly to the world beyond the school gates.”


Moira Marder, CEO of the Ted Wragg Trust, said: “This is an exceptional opportunity for Tor Bridge High and one that reflects our ambition to give every student access to meaningful experiences beyond the classroom.


“The project is rooted in Plymouth’s maritime context and will enable students to build confidence in mathematics and technical subjects while working alongside leading professionals. It is a powerful example of how schools and employers can work together to make future pathways visible and accessible.”


Phil Brown, Managing Director for Major Nuclear Capital Programmes Babcock said: “The future success of our industry depends on inspiring young people early and helping them see how their classroom learning connects to real-world careers. This programme gives students a practical insight into engineering while developing skills that will be valuable throughout their education and beyond.


“At Babcock, we’re committed to building the talent pipeline of the future. Initiatives like this, help demonstrate the exciting opportunities available across the defence and maritime sectors.”


Developed by AECOM in partnership with Class Of Your Own, the new Design a Port challenge forms part of the Design Engineer Construct! global learning programme. Through partnerships with industry and academia, the initiative gives students the opportunity to explore real-world applications of STEM while gaining insight into the diverse career pathways available across the built environment sectors.


*Students at Tor Bridge High School in Plymouth, part of the Ted Wragg Trust, set to participate in AECOM and Class of Your Own’s new STEM skills initiative.*


**About AECOM**


AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at[aecom.com](http://www.aecom.com/) .


**About Class Of Your Own**


Class Of Your Own (“COYO”) is an award-winning social enterprise founded in 2009 by Alison Watson MBE, creator of the ‘Design Engineer Construct!’ Learning Programme (“DEC”), a pioneering curriculum focusing on the digital Built Environment. By integrating STEM subjects and real-world project-based learning experiences, DEC educates and empowers children and young people to contribute positively to a net zero carbon future, giving them advanced skills and a deep understanding of design, engineering and construction concepts for a more sustainable world.
